title: Differential warmup profiles and soft failover spec
body:
Summary:

This spec proposes a system of differential warmup profiles plus a soft failover mechanism to reduce latency spikes and avoid disruptive preemptions when tenant demand suddenly increases. The intent is to give Dedicated customers predictable tail latency while preserving efficient utilization across pools. The feature sits in the autoscaling and routing layer and interacts with tenancy isolation controls and tenant-level SLO gates.

Background / motivation:
- Customers with reserved pools experience unpredictable cold starts when model KV caches and execution kernels need to ramp. Cold token latencies hurt UX and make SLOs harder to meet.
- Current reactive autoscaling adds capacity after latency breaches; this causes tail spikes.
- Hard preemption or immediate overcommit can cause noisy-neighbor incidents. We need graded responses that prioritize latency stability.

Goals:
- Provide tenant-configurable warmup profiles that shape how additional compute is provisioned and how traffic is routed into freshly-provisioned capacity.
- Implement a soft failover pathway that gracefully migrates traffic to compatible alternatives (slower model variant, lower-fidelity quantized model, or burst sandbox) when queues or per-tenant latency approach thresholds.
- Ensure observability and clear billing/chargeback signals for warmup and soft-failover events.

Non-goals:
- This is not a replacement for long-term capacity planning or reservations.
- Not addressing model training lifecycle or model artifact packaging (only serving/runtime behavior).

Design overview:
1) Warmup profiles
- Profiles are small JSON objects tenant can specify on Dedicated config: {target_qps_ramp, kv_prefetch, cache_prefetch_window_seconds, steady_state_batch_size_hint}.
- System maintains a per-tenant WarmState with phases: PREWARM -> RAMP -> STEADY -> COOLDOWN.
- PREWARM stage triggers KV/embedding cache fetches and proactive kernel selection for common sequence-length buckets. Limits: uses limited parallelism to avoid storming storage.
- RAMP stage increases concurrency and batch sizes gradually according to target_qps_ramp while tracking observed tail P95/P99.

2) Soft failover mesh
- When a tenant's latency budget (configurable SLO) is about to breach and warmstate is still RAMPING, orchestrator performs soft failover in this order (configurable): 1) route subset traffic to a compatible quantized variant (same accuracy tier), 2) route to a pre-authorized burst sandbox within the tenant's soft-claim bucket, 3) degrade fidelity by applying structured output length caps or beam-size caps.
- Each action has an associated cost multiplier and telemetry tag so billing/prod teams can reconcile cost vs. quality.

3) Isolation and admission gating:
- SLO gates: each tenant has gating thresholds (p95 latency warn, p99 breach). Warmup profiles include a gating_policy reference.
- Admission controller will, based on global load and pool headroom, decide whether to accept RAMP requests. If headroom low, orchestrator will solicit lender pools (opportunistic burst) only if tenant allows cross-pool borrowing.

API and UX:
- New fields on Dedicated tenant config endpoint (PATCH /v1/dedicated/tenants/:id): warmup_profile (string ref), allow_soft_failover (bool), fidelity_degradation_policy (enum), soft_burst_budget (seconds or token units).
- Console: per-tenant Warmup timeline visualization (phase, current ramp %, last prefetch time), per-tenant soft-failover history with reason tags and cost deltas.

Metrics / telemetry required:
- warmup.phase (PREWARM,RAMP,STEADY,COOLDOWN) with tenant id
- warmup.progress.percent
- softfailover.event{action,reason} with cost_multiplier and fallback_variant tag
- admission.rejects and admission.latency_blocked_reason
- per-tenant p50/p95/p99 and token-cost-increment attributed to soft failover events

Operational semantics and failure modes:
- If prefetch fails (e.g., KV store latency), fallback to conservative behaviour: hold in PREWARM and emit incident if > 30s.
- If warmup stalls while user traffic rises, soft failover triggers; if soft failover also unavailable, orchestrator engages protective throttling (rate limit) with explicit HTTP 429 and helpful Retry-After and hint fields.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (canary): implement warmup profile read-only + telemetry; run for 2 weeks on 10 internal tenants.
- Phase 1 (soft failover off): enable PREWARM and RAMP behaviors for 25% of staging traffic; measure tail reduction.
- Phase 2 (soft failover opt-in): allow select customers to opt into soft failover with billing flags.
- Phase 3 (default opt-out): after safety validation, expose as tenant-configurable default but require explicit billing consent for any cost multipliers.

Testing and validation:
- Create load generator scenarios that simulate sudden spike from 0->peak within 10s, 30s, 2m windows for multiple model families.
- Validate warmup reduces p99 by at least 30% for sequence lengths in the top 3 buckets.
- Chaos tests: simulate KV store slowdowns and ensure soft failover gracefully degrades.

Operational runbook highlights:
- Warmup stuck alert (warmup.phase stuck > 60s): triage KV store, kernel cache stats, and autoscaler logs. Use `warm-debug` tool to re-trigger prefetches.
- Softfailover cost spike: alert when softfailover.cost_multiplier_sum > threshold; rollback by toggling allow_soft_failover at tenant-level.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How aggressive should prefetch parallelism be without risking storage/CDN storms? (input from infra required).
- What fidelity-degradation operations are safe across all model families? Need research/ML to enumerate safe truncation/beam policies.
- Billing granularity for short soft-failover events — per-second or per-request multipliers? Finance input required.

Next steps:
- Engineering spike: prototype warmstate machine + small prefetcher library (2 sprints).
- ML research: produce fidelity degradation whitelist for top 8 model architectures (3 weeks).
- Product/legal: draft opt-in billing language and customer-facing help text.

Appendix: sample warmup_profile (human-readable)
- name: short-burst
- target_qps_ramp: 0->75% in 30s
- kv_prefetch: true
- cache_prefetch_window_seconds: 120
- steady_state_batch_size_hint: 8
